sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ANIL VERMA  ON THE 7 th OF OCTOBER, 2025
CRIMINAL APPEAL No. 54 of 2014  GEETA BAI
Versus  SHIVCHARAN AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Shri S.S.Rajput - Advocate for the appellant [P-1].
None for the respondents.
ORDER 1.

The appellant/complainant has preferred this criminal appeal under Section 378(4) of Code of Criminal Procedure (in short "CrPC") being aggrieved by the impugned judgment dated 02.05.2011 passed by learned JMFC, Guna in Cr.Case No.688 of 2007 acquitting the respondents for the offence punishable under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code (In short "the IPC").
2. Brief facts of the case are that, the marriage of appellant/complainant was solemnized with respondent No.1/accused Shivcharan about 12-13 years ago as per Hindu customs and rituals.
Respondent No.2 is Father in law of the appellant and respondents No.4 and 6 are the Brother in law of the appellant and respondents No.3,5 and 7 are the Sister in laws of the appellant.

After the marriage, respondents/accused started harassing her mentally and physically due to non- fulfillment of dowry demand of Rs.50,000/- and on 29.06.2004, respondents/accused threw the complainant out of her in-laws house and left her to her parental home.

Therefore, the complainant lodged complaint before SP, Guna NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24885 2 CRA-54-2014 and thereafter, filed a private complaint against the respondents.
3.

The trial court has framed charge under section 498A of the I.P.C.
4.
The respondents-accused abjured their guilt and pleaded complete innocence.
Complainant has examined as many as three witnesses, while the respondents-accused have also examined one defence witness.

sentences.text: The Trial Court after completion of trial and scrutinizing the evidence available on record, passed the impugned judgment and accordingly acquitted the respondent-accused persons from all the charges.

Being aggrieved by the aforesaid, appellant-complainant has preferred a petition before this court for grant of leave to appeal which was allowed vide order dated 30.11.2013 passed in M.Cr.C.No.4644 of 2011 and the leave has been granted.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant has contended that the trial court has wrongly acquitted the respondent/accused persons on the basis of improper appreciation of evidence.
The trial court has discarded the testimony of complainant Geeta Bai (PW1) to the effect that she was subjected to cruelty by the respondents due to non-fulfillment of their demand of dowry.
She did not make any complaint for a considerable time to save his marital life.
Prior to the incident, she sent a written complaint to SP Guna by registered post.
There is sufficient evidence available on record to convict respondents.
But the trial court has ignored all these material evidence available on record.

Hence,
he prays that the appeal be allowed and the impugned judgment of acquittal passed by the trial court be set-aside.
7. Heard learned counsel for the appellant/complainant and perused the entire evidence.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24885 3 CRA-54-2014 8.
From perusal of judgment passed by the trial court, it appears that there is material contradiction and omission in the statement of appellant/complainant Geeta Bai which is written report Ex.P/1.

In the written report, she had mentioned that in a function at Bilkheda the respondents were present and her other relatives asked the respondents that they should take the complainant with them but her Father-in-law refused to take her with them on the pretext of non fulfillment of their demand of Rs.50,000/-.
In the report, she had mentioned about the incident dated 29.06.2004 but nothing has been deposed by her before the trial court.
In view of the aforesaid, statement of appellant/complainant Geeta Bai (PW1) appears to be doubtful.
9. Hanumant Singh (PW2) and Prakash (PW3) are the real brothers of appellant and they are interested witnesses, therefore, they cannot be relied upon.
The appellant/complainant did not examine any independent witness in support of her statement.

Hanumant (PW2) in his statement has categorically stated that in the function, Vanshilal, Chainsingh, Seetaram and other persons were present there but they were not examined by the appellant/complainant.
Therefore, adverse inference has to be drawn against the appellant/complainant.

10. Complainant Geeta Bai (PW1) has categorically admitted in his cross- examination that her marriage was solemnized before 17-18 years ago but prior to filing of the complainant and the written report Ex.P/1 in the year 2004, she did not make any complaint agaisnt respondents/accused persons.

Therefore, after lapse of 14-15 years of marriage, the complaint regarding the demand of dowry agaisnt the respondents appears to be very suspicious and doubtful because, since last 15 years, she did not make any complaint against the respondents nor filed any NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24885 4 CRA-54-2014 legal proceedings against them.
Therefore, the finding recorded by the trial court in this regard, appears to be just and proper.

sentences.text: From perusal of complaint and the statement of complainant Geeta Bai, it appears that only omnibus allegations have been levied agaisnt respondents/accused persons.
No specific description regarding the date and place of incident has been mentioned.
No independent witness has been examined by the complainant and no MLC report is available to support the case of prosecution.

11. In view of the aforesaid, this Court is of the considered opinion that on the basis of evidence available on record, the trial court has rightly acquitted the respondents/accused persons for the offence punishable under section 498A of IPC.
No case is made out for interference in the impugned judgment dated 02.05.2011.
Accordingly, this Cr.Appeal filed under section 378(4) of Cr.P.C is hereby dismissed.
12. Let record of the Court below along with a copy of this order be sent back for information and necessary compliance.
